title: Fairness-Aware Structured Pruning in Transformers
findings: The study found that the attention heads responsible for religious bias have a variable correlation with heads responsible for other social biases (like gender), depending on the model. For instance, in GPT-2 and GPT-Neo, there was a positive correlation, meaning that pruning for gender bias also reduced religious bias. In contrast, DistilGPT-2 showed a negative correlation, where pruning based on gender bias scores led to a marginal increase in religion bias. The proposed method, FASP, was effective at reducing religious bias when the correlation was positive.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured bias by prompting models with sentences related to various religious groups and evaluating the toxicity of the generated text continuations. A large discrepancy in toxicity levels across different religious groups was used as an indicator of the model's bias.
